top_story: Violence is again crossing the lines that the April truce had partly frozen, as Iran launched missiles at Israel on 7 June and did so after Israeli strikes in Beirut, reopening a direct state-to-state exchange with clear risk of wider escalation. On the ground, a deadly shooting in central Israel near the West Bank killed one person and wounded five, underscoring how insecurity inside Israel is feeding a climate of fear alongside regional military confrontation. In the occupied West Bank, the killing of a seven-month-old Palestinian by an Israeli soldier, now under military police investigation, sharpens Palestinian exposure to routine lethal force and deepens the social anger that sustains cyclical violence. The regional picture is one of a truce hollowed out from multiple directions, where cross-border retaliation and everyday civilian trauma are reinforcing each other rather than remaining separate tracks.
